text:
incident-bot: INCIDENT 3012345678 — automated alert: sustained GPU queue growth in us-west2-serving (preemptible pool). Queue length >1200, worker backpressure, p95 latency spiking, 503 error rate increasing. Paging #incidents :rotating_light:

Oncall: I'm taking this. Noted the preemptible pool interruptions spike. @Alex Chen @Maria Gonzalez can you jump in?

Alex Chen: looking at autoscaler metrics — the cluster-autoscaler hit maxReplicas=40 and keeps failing to provision because cloud preemptible quota is saturated/instances aren't available. Spot interruption rate ~28% across nodes.

Maria Gonzalez: workload-queue reports backlog skewed to embedding jobs for 'vector-search' tenants. Fallback routing to dedicated pool appears to be OFF for some tenants due to a misguided feature flag rollout last week.

Sam Patel: starting quick checks. Running kubectl get hpa/deployment and checking autoscaler events.

Sam Patel: ```
kubectl get hpa -n serving
kubectl describe deployment vector-worker -n serving
# autoscaler events show "scaleUp forbidden: quota exceeded" and "insufficient capacity"
```

ops-runbook-bot: Runbook step 2 executed by Sam Patel: attempt emergency fallback routing. Command suggested: `curl -X POST https://controlplane.local/_admin/route/fallback -d '{"region":"us-west2","target":"dedicated-gpu-pool","selector":"priority<50"}'` — proceed with caution.

Alex Chen: cloud console shows reserved dedicated pool has 10 GPUs assigned. I can bump that to 20 temporarily but needs approval. Maria, if we enable fallback for low-priority tenants, we should throttle them to avoid saturating dedicated pool.

Maria Gonzalez: patching routing config for low-priority tenants now. Also applying a temporary rate-limit for non-enterprise tenants.

Maria Gonzalez: ```
# enable emergency fallback for selector=priority<50
curl -s -X POST https://controlplane.local/_admin/route/fallback \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \n  -d '{"region":"us-west2","target":"dedicated-gpu-pool","selector":"priority<50","max_rate":0.5}'
```

Lee Park: I'll throttle at the ingress layer as a second layer of protection. Applying nginx rate-limit for /v1/embeddings for non-zero-tenant-ids.

Support Bot: customer-impact summary: 12 tenants currently >10% error rate; 3 enterprise customers with moderate degradation. Status page updated: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/3012345678 — support team notified customers in the 500s and created support tickets.

Alex Chen: increased dedicated reserved pool from 10 -> 20 GPUs via infra console (approved). That freed capacity to accept rerouted jobs. Autoscaler still can't add more preemptible nodes due to cloud-side capacity but fallback is absorbing load.

Sam Patel: after enabling fallback and throttle, queue dropped from 1200 -> ~300 in 18 minutes. p95 latency back to ~1.4s for routed traffic. Error rate decreased. Monitoring for resurgence. :white_check_mark:

Oncall: deploying a short-lived policy to prefer dedicated pool for selector priority<70 while we stabilize. Leaving a note for night shift handoff.

Oncall: Handoff to night oncall @Lee Park at 3012345688. Open action items: 1) Evaluate why feature flag disabled fallback for subset of tenants; 2) Investigate autoscaler maxReplicas limits and cloud quota handling; 3) Improve capacity visibility for preemptible pools; 4) Postmortem and customer communication draft.

Lee Park: acknowledged. I'll keep the runbook open and continue to monitor for 2 hours, escalate if queue >500 or error rate rebounds.

ops-runbook-bot: Incident state: mitigated -> partial restore. Please add incident notes and follow-up tasks.

Alex Chen: quick note — possible root cause: combination of a recent feature-flag rollback (fallback disabled), a sudden regional spot interruption event, and conservative autoscaler max settings. We'll schedule a rollback-safe test and increase default emergency fallback coverage.

Support Bot: draft update for customers prepared, will be reviewed by Ops and sent after postmortem outline.

Oncall: closing the active paging loop. Will create a postmortem ticket and assign owners for the follow-ups. Thanks everyone for quick coordination. :heart:
